summary: A ghost: in early China the dead who are served in rites, or who return; in Buddhist translation, a whole realm of rebirth. The Shuowen glosses it by 歸, to return.
placement: Chosen by farthest-point sampling on the integrated Newton–Leipnik trajectory, so the eight stars spread across its projected shape. 魂 takes the highest of the eight points and 魄 the lowest, after the Liji’s 魂氣歸于天，形魄歸于地. A design choice, not a claim.

satellites.title: The Dead Are the Returned
satellites.evidence: The Shuowen glosses 鬼 by its near-homophone 歸, to return: 人所歸為鬼, “what people return to is 鬼”. To die is to go home, and the ghost is the one who has gone back.
satellites.caveat: A sound gloss (聲訓) is Han hermeneutics, not historical etymology. Wording from general knowledge.
